item.title: Agentic RAG vs. Plain Hybrid RAG: What My Hydropower Benchmark Revealed
item.guid: title:agentic rag vs plain hybrid rag what my hydropower benchmark revealed
item.description: Most RAG applications follow a simple path: Retrieve a few documents → send them to an LLM → generate an answer. That works for straightforward lookup questions. But it becomes fragile when the question spans multiple manuals, needs numerical reasoning, contains tables, or asks for an engineering recommendation grounded in plant documentation. I built an Agentic RAG system for Small Hydropower Plant (SHP) engineering to explore a harder question: Can a multi-agent retrieval workflow improve the quality of answers from private technical documents without depending on paid inference APIs? The answer, based on my evaluation so far, is nuanced: it improves retrieval precision, but comes with a substantial latency cost and does not automatically outperform a well-designed plain RAG pipeline on faithfulness. The complete implementation is available here: Agentic RAG for Small Hydropower .

item.title: Your agent traces are a secret store: notes on the Cursor, Apify and Epoch AI incident reports
item.guid: title:your agent traces are a secret store notes on the cursor apify and epoch ai incident reports
item.description: On 13 November 2026, Cursor, Apify and Epoch AI each published an incident report. At VSO we check AI-related incidents against primary sources before we write about them, and a monitoring brief had grouped these three as "AI agent incidents". They are three different kinds of event. This post goes through what the primary sources say, then pulls out the engineering points that matter if you build with agents. Cursor: credentials in shared agent traces Cursor's 13 November update explains the tampered extension build it disclosed in October. Per Cursor: Cursor had issued an access key to Fireworks AI, one of its inference vendors.

item.title: Post-training Stages and Preference Data — It is much easier to judge than to generate
item.guid: title:post training stages and preference data it is much easier to judge than to generate
item.description: Goal: understand the stages of LLM post-training, then what preferences are, why post-training needs them, and how preference data is collected. Part 1: Post-training Stages 1. Pre-training builds knowledge, post-training builds behavior • Pre-training: the model reads a huge amount of text and learns to predict the next word, which gives it knowledge but no manners. • Post-training: it takes far less compute, yet largely decides how well a model follows instructions, how safe it is and how it reasons (Developers Digest, n. d. ).

item.title: Your Traces Are Evidence: Retention, Legal Hold, and Discovery for Agent Logs
item.guid: title:your traces are evidence retention legal hold and discovery for agent logs
item.description: The flight recorder you built for debugging has a second reader. Retention policy, legal hold, and what not to write down. Image 01: The Second Reader- When Agent Traces Become Legal Evidence (Image by Author) The discovery request, in this composite drawn from several teams’ first encounters with litigation, was one sentence long: produce all records of automated decision-making concerning the plaintiff, including system logs, for the relevant period. The team’s first reaction was relief. They had the records — of course they had the records. This series had convinced them years earlier: trace everything, don’t sample , keep the full span tree, every prompt, every tool call, every model response.

item.title: Introducing WorldVQA
item.guid: title:introducing worldvqa
item.description: A benchmark for evaluating atomic visual world knowledge in Multimodal LLMs. Authors Kimi Team We are releasing WorldVQA , a new benchmark designed to measure the factual correctness of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). While recent models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in visual reasoning and description, measuring their reliability regarding visual world knowledge remains a challenge.
